  "text": "By morning, the tide had left a line of seaweed across the square. Mara found the harbor master sweeping it into a pile beside the streetlamp. The gate stood open behind him.

“I thought you secured it,” she said.

“We did.” He leaned on the broom. “The chain was still fastened when I came down. But the gate was open, and the chain was hanging from the wall.”

Mara looked toward the highest step. The shell was gone.

The woman appeared at the quay carrying two cups of tea. She handed one to Mara and kept the other warm between her palms.

“Did the girl come back?” Mara asked.

“No.”

“Then why are you here?”

The woman glanced at the open gate. “I wanted to see what you remembered.”

Mara sat on the step. She could recall the child’s cold fingers around hers, but nothing after the bell. She had always believed she let go. Last night, when the child passed her in the square, Mara had been too afraid to ask.

“I pulled her through, didn’t I?”

The woman nodded. “Then you went back down for the photograph.”

Mara looked up. “What photograph?”

“The one she was holding.”

The harbor master reached into his coat and drew out a damp square of paper he had found beneath the streetlamp. In it, a little girl stood on the highest step beside Mara. The harbor was behind them, bright with sun.

Mara took the photograph. On the back, in a child’s careful writing, were three words: You came back."
